title: UK Warns Visa Applicants: Don't Book Travel Until Your Decision Arrives
excerpt: Home Office updates both processing-time pages to state UKVI will not cover travel costs if applications are refused or delayed.
body:
• The UK Home Office updated its visa processing-time guidance on September 9, 2026, warning applicants not to book travel to the UK until they receive a visa decision.
  • UKVI now states it will not be responsible for any travel costs or expenses incurred if a visa application is refused or takes longer than expected.
  • The same clarification was added to both the outside-the-UK and inside-the-UK processing-times pages on GOV.UK.
  • Standard processing remains 3 weeks for most visas applied for outside the UK, and up to 8 weeks for applications made inside the UK.

The UK Home Office has tightened its visa processing guidance, explicitly warning applicants not to book travel to the UK until they have received a decision — and making clear it will not cover costs if applications are refused or delayed.

The update, published on September 9, 2026, appears on both GOV.UK guidance pages: "Visa processing times: applications outside the UK" and "Visa processing times: applications inside the UK."

What changed

On the outside-the-UK page, the new wording states: "You should not book your travel until you get a decision on your visa application" and adds that "UKVI will not be responsible for any expenses or travel costs incurred if your visa processing time takes longer than expected."

The inside-the-UK page carries near-identical language: applicants "should not book travel to the UK until you have received a decision on your visa," and UKVI "will not reimburse any travel costs or other expenses if your application is refused or takes longer than expected."

Why it matters for Indian applicants

India remains one of the largest sources of UK visa applicants — across student, skilled worker, visitor and family routes. Applicants commonly book flights and accommodation around expected decision dates, particularly ahead of university terms and the festive travel season. The updated guidance puts the financial risk squarely on applicants: non-refundable bookings made before a decision arrives will not be compensated, even if UKVI itself runs past its published processing times.

Standard processing times are unchanged: most visas applied for outside the UK are decided within 3 weeks, while family visas take 12 weeks. Applications made inside the UK generally take 8 weeks, with some routes such as Health and Care Worker and Start-up decided in 3 weeks.

What applicants should do

The practical advice is straightforward: wait for the decision letter or email before booking anything non-refundable. If faster processing is needed, UKVI notes applicants "may be able to pay for a faster decision" on some routes — though priority services are not available for every category. And applicants should not contact UKVI to chase an application that is still within its published processing time; the office says it cannot provide status updates in that window.
